question: Refer to the exhibit. What is the result of implementing this configuration?
context:
NEXUS(config)# feature tacacs+
NEXUS(config)# tacacs-server timeout 5
NEXUS(config)# tacacs-server directed-request
NEXUS(config)# tacacs-server deadtime 0
NEXUS(config)# tacacs-server host 10.1.50.20 port 49
NEXUS(config)# tacacs-server host 10.1.50.20 key 7 "F1whg123" timeout 1
NEXUS(config)# aaa group server tacacs+ ISE
NEXUS(config-tacacs+)# server 10.1.50.20
NEXUS(config-tacacs+)# deadtime 10
NEXUS(config-tacacs+)# use-vrf management
NEXUS(config-tacacs+)# source-interface mgmt 0
NEXUS(config)# aaa authentication login default group ISE
options: The switch queries the TACACS+ server by using an encrypted text PAP login.
The TACACS+ server uses the type-6 encrypted format.
The switch queries the TACACS+ server by using a clear text PAP login.
The timeout value on the TACACS+ server is 10 seconds.
theory: TACACS+ encrypts the entire body of every packet exchanged between the switch and the server - not just the password, as RADIUS does - so even though the login exchange functionally resembles a simple username/password (PAP-style) prompt, the query the switch sends to the ISE TACACS+ server (10.1.50.20, group ISE) is fully encrypted end to end. This confidentiality advantage over RADIUS is the key reason TACACS+ is generally preferred for administrative AAA on Nexus devices. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 18 - AAA, TACACS+ vs. RADIUS)
